expected_level_description: You can: - lead the organisation's medium-term financial plan - align financial plans with strategy, workforce, and investment plans - advise the board on financial sustainability and the choices needed to stay within funding - set the planning assumptions and methods used across the organisation

You can: - set the organisation's business case and investment appraisal standards - advise investment boards on affordability, value for money, and risk - make the case to funders for major investment programmes - review the portfolio of investments and recommend where to stop, change, or continue

You can: - own the organisation's financial rules and scheme of delegation - report to the audit committee on financial control and audit actions - lead the response to significant control failures or fraud - build a culture where staff understand their duty to use public money properly

You can: - represent the organisation with funders and oversight bodies - advise the board on regularity, propriety, and value for money - shape funding agreements and financial regimes for the organisation's services
You can: - influence or create complex budgets across an organisation, programme or product view - manage the budget you are given and make it work

skill: Financial management for digital, data and technology
expected_level_description: *Senior leadership skill: the UK GDaD PCF defines it with one statement, not by level.* You can: - own, manage and optimise budgets across digital, data and technology - secure appropriate investment to deliver organisational strategy and priorities - negotiate investments in shared technologies across the organisation and across government Examples of leadership using this skill: - prioritising competing demands for investment in people, infrastructure and innovation across digital, data and technology to maximise value - identifying risk to critical services and influencing stakeholders to increase investment to ensure they are maintained - balancing short-term tactical gains with longer-term strategies to ensure value now and in the future

You can: - develop and own a business case and iterate it throughout the life cycle - coach others on identifying benefits whilst balancing user and business needs - communicate the delivery of incremental value - build the case for an organisational approach to value through product strategy - coach and empower teams to take a value for money approach

You can: - direct the stakeholder relationship strategy for your teams - ensure stakeholder's objectives are set and support teams to meet them - influence and negotiate with senior stakeholders to resolve issues and enable progress

You can: - change organisational structures to fixable and sustainable designs - lead on the strategy for the whole organisation, marrying business needs with innovative analysis - make and justify decisions characterised by high levels of risk, impact and complexity - build consensus between organisations (private or public) or highly independent and diverse stakeholders - solve and unblock issues between teams or departments at the highest level - understand the psychology of a team and have strong mediation skills - coach the organisation on team dynamics and conflict resolution
You can: - lead managers and shape the culture of a large area - design workforce plans and organisational change - coach leaders and resolve complex people issues
